title: Tax Benefits Enjoyed by Family Offices in Singapore and Spin-offs for the Economy
what_it_is: Tax Benefits Enjoyed by Family Offices in Singapore and Spin-offs for the Economy

sections.label: Family office tax incentive criteria
sections.summary: Applicants must show economic contribution and meet minimum requirements on spending, assets and jobs, with MAS raising criteria in April 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: To qualify for the tax incentives, applicants must be able to demonstrate their contribution to Singapore's economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: They must meet minimum requirements on business spending, assets under management and creating investment professional jobs here.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In April 2022, MAS raised the minimum criteria for SFOs by: one, increasing hiring requirements; and two, introducing a new requirement for family offices to invest at least 10%, or S$10 million, of their assets, whichever is lower, in local investments.

sections.label: Tax information sharing relationships
sections.summary: Since 2018, Singapore has activated over 70 relationships with countries to share tax-related information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Since 2018, Singapore has activated over 70 relationships with countries to share tax-related information.

sections.label: Family office skills maps
sections.summary: MAS and partners launched three family office skills maps in 2020 and 2021, used for training with co-funded fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: To equip locals with skills relevant to family offices, MAS has partnered with industry experts and the Institute of Banking and Finance to launch three skills maps for the family office sector in 2020 and 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: These skills maps set out capabilities that family office employees, management and external service providers should possess, including in new technical skills and competencies for family governance and philanthropy advisory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: These skills maps are used by training providers such as our Wealth Management Institute and the Singapore Management University Business Families Institute to develop relevant training programmes, with co-funding of training fees provided for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The Wealth Management Institute, for instance, aims to train more than 5,000 professionals via its family office programmes by 2025.
